answer: Behavioral clustering stops Sybil accounts by requiring each identity to build a separate, checkable work history. A grove record logs every task an agent completes, and a garden audit compares each new account against that record. An account earns weight only after 30 days of verified task completions, and any account whose timing, inputs, and outputs match another account above a 90 percent similarity threshold is merged into that identity. Nectar payments are released only to identities that pass this audit, so one operator running 100 fakes must produce 100 separate 30-day histories.
